outside.says: Onboarded holders, under the PPM of their own offering: normal redemption up to T+3 US business days through a FIFO queue that burns the token; an experimental instant USDC route on selected chains is liquidity-limited and excess requests queue. 5bp redemption fee; 30bp annual TER.
The US and Non-US agreements incorporate different offering documents; the governing one is decided by the holder's onboarding, not by the token.

OpenEden's docs describe a multisig, a treasury timelock and administrator oversight; redemptions burn the token. None of this was read on chain (the only token is an Ethereum ERC-20), and the powers the PPM grants were not reviewed.
The docs name sovereign, market and liquidity risks; insolvency priority and recovery of the interest are not established.

verdict.summary: Two token declarations by two named issuer entities over one contract, with a researcher's flag between them, says the documented inconsistency exactly. The holder's interest, the controlling register and the fund units still need proposals, and the token is an EVM contract. The custodian, administrator, auditor and counsel are all unnamed, so only the issuer side and OpenEden speak.
